data.headline: Rip Current Statement issued October 20 at 2:19AM EDT until October 22 at 8:00PM EDT by NWS Miami FL
data.description:
* WHAT...Dangerous rip currents expected.

* WHERE...Coastal Palm Beach County, Coastal Broward County and
Coastal Miami Dade County.

* WHEN...Through Thursday evening.

* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water.
data.instruction:
Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

FXUS62 KMFL 201135
AFDMFL

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Miami FL
735 AM EDT Tue Oct 20 2026

...New AVIATION...

.KEY MESSAGES...
Updated at 732 AM EDT Tue Oct 20 2026

 - Hazardous marine conditions continue today for the Atlantic and
   Gulf waters. High risk of rip currents remains in place for the
   Atlantic beaches. 

 - Dangerous surf conditions today for the Palm Beach and Broward
   beaches.

 - Minor to moderate coastal flooding possible mid to late week.

&&

.SHORT TERM...
(Today through Wednesday)
Issued at 103 AM EDT Tue Oct 20 2026

Latest analysis shows a stalled frontal boundary along the FL 
Straits, surface low pressure well off the Mid Atlantic coast, and 
strong high pressure over eastern Canada. At the upper levels, there 
is ridging over the center of the country and upper level lows off 
both coasts of the US. Overall, the pattern won't change much today 
or Wednesday. Latest 00Z sounding shows a lot of mid and upper level 
dry air and forecast soundings show the dry air aloft remaining in 
place. There will be enough low level moisture in place with the 
steady N/NE breeze for widely scattered showers to continue across 
the east coast metro, with overall fairly dry conditions over the 
interior and SW FL. 

High temperatures both today and Wednesday will be in the low to 
middle 80s across the east coast metro and around Lake Okeechobee, 
and mid to upper 80s over SW FL and the southern Everglades. Low 
temperatures tonight will range from the low to middle 60s across SW 
FL, to upper 60s and lower 70s across SE FL. 

&&

.LONG TERM...
(Wednesday night through Monday)
Issued at 103 AM EDT Tue Oct 20 2026

As we head towards the end of the work week, heights continue to 
fall across the region and eventually an upper level low will form 
in the vicinity of Cuba over the weekend. Wrap around moisture will 
increase rain chances, especially across the east coast metro. In 
addition to the higher rain chances, the pressure gradient will 
tighten once again as strong high pressure builds into New England. 
Expect breezy NE winds this weekend into early next week, with early 
indications of wind gusts of 30-40 mph possible, especially along 
the coast. 

High temperatures during the extended period will be fairly 
consistent, ranging from the low to middle 80s each day. Overnight 
temps will be in the 60s/70s. 

&&

.AVIATION...
(12Z TAFS)
Issued at 732 AM EDT Tue Oct 20 2026

VFR conditions will prevail throughout the forecast period. NE
winds will increase after 15z and range between 10 to 15 kts 
through the afternoon hours. Wind gusts of 20 to 25 kts will be
possible across all terminals after 15z. Scattered showers will
remain possible near the east coast terminals mainly through the
early afternoon hours. 

&&

.MARINE...
Issued at 103 AM EDT Tue Oct 20 2026

Hazardous marine conditions will continue through mid week with NE 
winds 20-25 kts today decreasing to 15-20 kts on Wednesday. Seas in 
the Atlantic 8-12 ft today decreasing to 4-8 ft on Wednesday. Seas 
in the Gulf 3-6 ft today and 1-3 ft on Wednesday. Hazardous seas 
will likely linger in portions of the Atlantic waters through the 
end of the week, and then hazardous conditions for all local waters 
are expected this weekend as an upper level low forms to our south 
in the Caribbean and the pressure gradient locally tightens.

&&

.BEACHES...
Issued at 103 AM EDT Tue Oct 20 2026

Strong NE flow and dangerous swell will result in a high risk of rip 
currents continuing for the Atlantic coast through at least 
Thursday. In addition, large breaking waves in the surf zone is 
expected along the Palm Beach coast through Wednesday morning and 
Broward coast through this evening. 

With the upcoming King Tide cycle, minor to moderate coastal 
flooding is possible beginning mid week and lasting through at least 
the upcoming weekend around the high tide cycles each day.

&&

TWOAT 

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
800 AM EDT Tue Oct 20 2026

For the North Atlantic...Caribbean Sea and the Gulf of America:

Off the East Coast of the United States (AL93):
A storm-force non-tropical low pressure area located a few hundred 
miles off the North Carolina coast is producing some shower and 
thunderstorm activity primarily west of its center. However, 
overnight satellite wind data indicated the low was still attached 
to an occluded front. Over the next couple of days, the low could 
develop some organized deep convection and gradually lose its 
frontal features while it moves slowly north-northeastward over the 
Gulf Stream, allowing the system to briefly develop subtropical 
characteristics. By the end of the week, the system is expected to 
accelerate northeastward away from the the eastern United States, 
where environmental conditions are expected to become unfavorable 
for additional subtropical or tropical development. 

Regardless of the status of the system, high winds, coastal 
flooding, and dangerous surf are expected along portions of the U.S. 
East Coast during the next few days. For more information, please 
consult statements and warnings from local National Weather Service 
offices and the Weather Prediction Center, along with High Seas 
Forecasts and Storm Warnings issued by the National Weather Service.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...medium...40 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...medium...40 percent.

&&
High Seas Forecasts issued by the National Weather Service can be 
found under AWIPS header NFDHSFAT1, WMO header FZNT01 KWBC, and 
online at ocean.weather.gov/shtml/NFDHSFAT1.php

$$
Forecaster Papin
